candidates.name: Sturge-Weber syndrome
support_spans: bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve
iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and evenly distributed micronodular elevations on the iris surface
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of bilateral naevus flammeus and iris heterochromia is consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

candidates.name: Glaucoma
support_spans: intraocular pressure measured by Icare tonometry was 22 mm Hg in the right eye
gonioscopy demonstrated open angles bilaterally with diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye
candidates.why: The elevated intraocular pressure and trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye suggest glaucoma.

candidates.name: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
support_spans: bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of bilateral naevus flammeus may be related to an underlying vascular malformation, as seen in Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome.

candidates.name: Sturge-Weber syndrome

candidates.why: The patient's presentation of iris heterochromia and naevus flammeus is consistent with the leptomeningeal angioma calcification syndrome, also known as Sturge-Weber syndrome.

candidates.name: Ocular melanosis
support_spans: iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and evenly distributed micronodular elevations on the iris surface
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of iris heterochromia and hyperpigmentation may be related to ocular melanosis, which can be confirmed with histopathological examination.

candidates.name: Choroidal hemangioma
support_spans: increased retinal vessel tortuosity and a diffusely darker fundus in the right eye
B-scan ultrasonography measured choroidal thickness of 2.2 mm in the right eye versus 1.4 mm in the left
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of increased retinal vessel tortuosity and choroidal thickening may be related to a choroidal hemangioma, which can be confirmed with imaging studies.
